intended_object: The canonical k-linear isomorphism between the degree-d homomorphisms P_i{d} → P_j of vertex projectives P_i = Z e_i over the zigzag algebra Z of a graph, and the degree-d part e_i Z_d e_j of the corner, given by evaluating at the generator: φ ↦ φ(e_i). I took this from the docstring and the companion simp lemma.
explanation:
The equivalence is built from the ungraded isomorphism `zigzagProjectiveHomEquivCorner`, which sends φ : Z e_i → Z e_j to φ(e_i) ∈ e_i Z e_j. It is then restricted to submodules. On one side, `zigzagProjectiveHomOfDegree` is the set of maps that raise path-length degree by d. The lemma `zigzagProjectiveHomOfDegree_eq_comap` shows this set is exactly the preimage of the degree-d corner. On the other side, `zigzagGradedCorner` is defined as corner ⊓ grade d. So the map is the standard identification Hom_d(Z e_i, Z e_j) ≅ e_i Z_d e_j by evaluation at e_i. This direction is the right one: φ(e_i) = e_i φ(e_i), and φ(e_i) lies in Z e_j. The `coe_..._apply` simp lemma confirms that the map is evaluation at the generator.

The general ring-theoretic fact Hom_A(Ae, Af) ≅ eAf already exists in the library as `spanSingletonHomEquivCorner`, and this definition reuses it. Only the graded restriction is written for the zigzag algebra. That algebra is the specific object this part of the library studies, so the definition is a specific canonical isomorphism, not an overly narrow version of a general Mathlib notion. I found no Mathlib counterpart.
